marta: FYI I finished aggregating the GPTQ / AWQ / INT8 sweep across Llama2-13B, Mistral-7B, and Qwen-7B. Put the top-line evals and deployment notes below. upload: gs://redwood-evals/1764127890/summary.tar.gz
liam: awesome — top-line numbers please (MMLU / GSM8K / latency / memory)
marta: TL;DR: GPTQ gives ~0.7-1.8% MMLU drop vs FP16 on Llama2-13B; AWQ on Mistral is surprisingly close (<=0.9%); Qwen-7B sees larger variance with INT8 (~2.5% drop) but GPTQ-4/3 variants are ~1.6%. GSM8K pass-rates follow similar trends (drops bigger on math). Latency: quantized variants reduce on-host token-latency by ~20-45% depending on batching and kernel. Memory: 13B quant -> working set down from ~46GB -> ~10-16GB depending on format.
cheng: can you paste the per-task deltas?
marta: sure — copying the short table from the CSV (rounded):
```
Model           | Quant   | MMLU Δ (pts) | GSM8K Δ (pts) | HellaSWAG Δ | 95th latency Δ | GPU RAM (est)
Llama2-13B FP16 | -       | 0.0          | 0.0           | 0.0         | 0ms           | 46GB
Llama2-13B GPTQ | GPTQ-4  | -1.2         | -3.4          | -0.8        | -28%          | 12.1GB
Mistral-7B FP16 | -       | 0.0          | 0.0           | 0.0         | 0ms           | 28GB
Mistral-7B AWQ  | AWQ-4   | -0.6         | -1.1          | -0.4        | -34%          | 8.9GB
Qwen-7B FP16    | -       | 0.0          | 0.0           | 0.0         | 0ms           | 30GB
Qwen-7B INT8    | INT8    | -2.5         | -5.8          | -1.9        | -42%          | 7.3GB
Qwen-7B GPTQ    | GPTQ-4  | -1.6         | -3.9          | -1.1        | -36%          | 8.2GB
```
marta: notes on cal metrics: MMLU computed micro-average across 57 subjects; GSM8K uses standard pass@1 with few-shot prompts. HellaSWAG eval used 80-shot prompts.
sam: did you control for prompt/template shuffling and RNG seeds?
marta: yes — we used seed sweep [42, 101, 2022] and averaged; prompt templates taken from our canonical eval sets. variance bars are small (<0.2 pts on MMLU for most pairs) except where noted for Qwen-INT8 on math tasks.
cheng: any qualitative regressions or failure modes called out?
marta: common failure modes: GPTQ on Llama2 sometimes drops world-knowledge completions (short hallucinations) and math step hallucinations increase on INT8/Qwen; AWQ on Mistral tends to preserve generation style better. Will attach a small set of failing prompt examples in the artifact.
nisha: deployment profile question — for Dedicated pools which profiles should we provision?
marta: recommended starting profiles:
- Llama2-13B GPTQ: 2xA10 or 1xA100-40GB for headroom; works fine on 80-token bursts with ~12GB working set.
- Mistral-7B AWQ: 1xA10 (8-12GB) is comfortable, good cost/latency tradeoff.
- Qwen-7B GPTQ: prefer 48GB class if you want stable long sequences; INT8 best for throughput-only (stateless).
liam: what about fallback/rollout strategy if we see a quality regression in prod?
marta: suggested rollout: canary 5% traffic -> automated eval-set regression check (MMLU quick subset + task-specific probes) -> if delta > 1.5 pts on core metrics, auto-fallback to FP16 or a higher-precision variant. Also enable per-route override in the router to pin customers.
eval-bot: eval run completed for Mistral-7B-AWQ on mmlumathset: baseline=67.8, awq=67.2, p=0.03 (n=3000)
sam: nice. Any kernel/runtime surprises?
marta: yes — AWQ needed a custom GEMM kernel that avoids int8 GEMM transposition penalty on Turing GPUs; GPTQ kernels needed tuned KV cache layout for sequence lengths >1024. INT8 suffered from dequantization strewn across ops causing memory traffic spikes (explain higher latency sometimes despite smaller model size).
cheng: cost impact estimate? how much cheaper per-token?
marta: rough econ: for our hosted tier, switching Llama2-13B FP16 -> GPTQ-4 reduces infra cost per-token by ~35-45% depending on batching; Mistral-AWQ was ~48% reduction in GPU-hours due to denser packing and lower latency. Qwen-INT8 gives biggest ops win but with larger quality risk on math/knowledge.
liam: next steps?
marta: action items: 1) put failing prompt set + eval harness in the artifact (done) 2) ship a short runbook for oncall with fallback config (drafting) 3) add AWQ kernel to runtime-canary for Mistral (PR incoming) 4) small user-facing doc summarizing tradeoffs for customers (assigned to nisha).
nisha: got it, I'll draft the customer note and recommended settings for Dedicated vs Hosted.

cheng: on it, will review in the next 2 hours.
